    Instructions:

          If any assumptions are required, assume the same and mention those assumptions in the answer script.
        Use of intelligence is highly appreciated.
        Mention the question number in the text cell and next ’code cell’ shall contain the code related to the
      respective question.
         All your inferences shall be put in the text cell with the respective question number.
       You are requested to convert interactive python note book (ipynb) into a pdf file (single file) and upload
      in python



 Instructions

Platform and Format

        Use Jupyter Notebook for this lab examination.

        For each question:

      – Type the question exactly as given in the question paper.

      – Add explanation describing your logic required for the question.

      – Write your code in the following cell(s).

      – Display the output immediately below the corresponding code cell.

      – Add a subsection titled “AI Log for the question” after the output. “AI Log” should include:
           *           The prompt(s) you used for the question.
           *            Print  of the AI-tool’s response.


    Submission Format

         1. After completing the exam:

          – Save your notebook as a PDF showing questions, code, outputs, and explanations clearly.
               *                  In Jupyter: File →Download as →PDF

         2. Name your file as:

         <RegisterNumber>_PAMCA504-W26.pdf

         3. Upload the single PDF file through the link provided in MS-Team
 
    Output and Code Requirements

      – Submissions containing only outputs without code will be treated as invalid.

      – Code, output, and explanation,AI-log must be clearly visible in the PDF.

      – Full marks will be awarded only if both code and corresponding output are present.

    For every question, Jupyter notebook, should have the following components

      – Question No, Question description

      – Explanation of the code

      – Code

      – Output

      – Details of AI usage


    AI-Tool Usage and Logging

         1. You may use AI tools only as assistive references, not for direct copy-paste.

         2. For each question, if you used any AI tool:

          – The prompt(s) you used for the question.
          – Print  of the AI-tool’s response.

         3. Example format:

         AI Log for Question 3:
         Prompt: Explain k-means clustering initialization.
         AI Response: Described k-means++ method with sklearn example.
         % My use: Adapted the code for the given dataset; changed n_clusters=4.

          If you did not use any AI tool for a question, write:


     AI Log for Question 3: No AI tool used.

        At the end of your notebook, include a final section titled:


     Complete AI-Assistance Log

       listing all prompts and corresponding responses used across the exam.

Academic Integrity

        Submissions with fabricated outputs, copied code, or undeclared AI assistance will be treated
      as malpractice.

        Your notebook must reflect your own understanding and analysis.

Submission Checklist

Before submitting, for each question, please ensure the following:

        Question typed

       Code included

        Output visible

        Explanation written


                                               2
 
        AI log (per question) added

        Saved and uploaded as single PDF

   You are provided with a dataset that bears your roll.no as the file-name of the dataset. Before the start
of the examination, please check whether you have got a dataset which has your roll.no. Your data set is
referred as dataset D.

   1. Data Preprocessing (with the dataset D)                                                     [15 marks]

       (a) Check the dimension and display the first 15 records of the dataset.                        [1 mark]

      (b) Identify the NaN values in each of the input, output the number of NaN values in each of the input
           attributes.                                                                                         [1 mark]

       (c) Identify the attributes which follow normal distribution                                     [2 marks]

      (d) Do the imputation by replacing all the NaN values in an attribute with the mean of all the values of
          that attribute or mode of all the values of that attribute. After executing the imputation, confirm
          that the imputation gets reflected in the dataset with appropriate outputs.               [2 marks]

       (e) Identify the outliers in each of the attribute and replace the outliers using the ‘capping process’.[2
          marks]

        (f) Caluclate the Maximum and Minimum value for each of attributes of D.                   [1 mark]

       (g) From the dataset D, prepare a new dataframe, called as the ‘D-test-data’, as follows:
                          All the input attributes of D will be the columns of ‘D-test-data’.
                          ’D-test-data’ will not have the target column of D
                          ’D-test-data’ will have 15 rows.
                       None of the values in any row of D-test-data will be as the rows of D.
                               If (a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, a6, a7, a8, a9) is a row in D-test-data,with ai as the value in the Ai column
                of D (i = 1 to 9), ai should not be present in the Ai column of D (in any row) and ai should
             be between the maximum value of the entries in the Ai column and the minimum value of the
                entries in the Ai column. For example, if (2, 3.1, 4.5, 5, 9, 0.1, 5, 8.1, 9.0) is a row in D-test-data,
               there should not be any rows (excludng the value in target column of D) in D  , with the
              corresponding values (2, 3.1, 4.5, 5, 9, 0.1, 5, 8.1, 9.0) and all the entries should be between the
             max.value and the min.value of the respective columns in D
                         In short, If you super-impose (place over) a row (a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, a6, a7, a8, a9) of D-test-data
            on any row of D (with out the target column entry ), there should be a mismatch in all the
               values (a, i is from 1 to 9)
                                                                                                                [6 marks]

   2. Training the models                                                                          [25 marks]

       (a) With 75% of the dataset D, conduct the following experiments.

                    i. Train a multiple linear regression model with a polynomial of degree 1 (with all the terms) by
               considering all the input features of the dataset D and execute the following experiments E1,
           E2 ,E3.                                                                                       [6 marks]
             A. Experiment 1 (E1): Optimization strategy should be ‘Stochastic Gradient Descent’.
                                 Compute the error in E1 due to the training data and the error due to validation data.
                                   Based on the learning of your model, predict the output of the datapoints in ‘D-test-
                     data’ and append a new column with the predicted output and name the column as
                SGD. Print the D-test-data with the output.
              B. Experiment 2 (E2): Optimization strategy should be ‘Batch Gradient Descent’.
                                 Compute the error in E2 due to the training data and the error due to validation data.
                                   Based on the learning of your model, predict the output of the datapoints in ‘D-test-
                     data’ and append a new column with the predicted output and name the column as
               BGD. Print the D-test-data with the output.


                                               3
 
C. Experiment 3 (E3): Optimization strategy should be ‘Mini-batch Gradient Descent’.
       Compute the error in E3 due to the training data and the error due to validation data.
        Based on the learning of your model, predict the output of the datapoints in ‘D-test-data’
     and append a new column with the predicted output and name the column as MGD.
      Print the D-test-data with the output.
D. Experiment 4 (E4): Generate a new data set (D1) from the data set D such that D1 has
    labled outputs where the labels (for the outputs)are assigned as follows.          [4 marks]
        For the output values ≤0, assign the label Z
        For the output values such that 0 < output value ≤10, assign the label B
        For the output values such that 10 < output value ≤20, assign the label C.
        For the output values such that 20 < output value ≤30, assign the label D
        For the output values > 30, assign the label E
   Thus, D1 is obtained from D, just by replacing the values in the output column of D with
   the respective labels assigned to them and all the values of all the other input attributes
    of D will also be in D1.
E. Experiment 5 (E5) : Generate a new data set D2 from D1 as described.          [5 marks]
         Scale the attributes using standardisation scalar if the attributes follow normal distri-
     bution and scale the attributes using normalization scalar if the attributes do not follow
     normal distribution.
        Check whether the data set is balanced or not. For a k-class dataset, each class shall
     have approximately  k data points, where N is the total number of data points in the                   N
      dataset D1. If the dataet is imbalanced, balance the dataset D1.
         After scaling the attributes and balancing the data set, Let us call the balanced and
      standardised data set as D2.
   You have to do any TWO EXPERIMENTS from E6,E7,E8             [6 marks]
F. Experiment 6 (E6): Using the labled dataset D2, Train a logistic regression learning model
    for classification
        Generate the accuracy and the classification report on the learning of the logistic regres-
      sion model.
        Based on the learning of your model, predict the output of the datapoints in ‘D-test-
      data’ and append a new column with the predicted output and name the output column
      as LR . Print the D-test-data with the output.
G. Experiment 7 (E7): Using the labled dataset D2, Train a tree-based non-parametric learn-
    ing model for classification
        Generate the accuracy and the classification report on the learning of the tree-based
     model.
        Based on the learning of your model, predict the output of the datapoints in ‘D-test-
      data’ and append a new column with the predicted output and name the output column
      as DT. Print the D-test-data with the output.
H. Experiment 8 (E8): Train the SVM classifier with the data set D2, as follows.
         Print the support vectors of the model.
        Generate the accuracy and the classification report on the learning of the SVM model.
        Based on the learning of your model, predict the output of the datapoints in ‘D-test-
      data’ and append a new column with the predicted output and name the output column
      as SVM . Print the D-test-data with the output.
       Compute the accuracy measure ( with the validation data set) of the classifier.
         Print the confusion matrix and generate the classification report of your experiment.
 I. Experiment 09 (E09): Remove the Target column of D2 and obtain a new data set D3.
   Train the K-means clustering model with the data set D3.                         [4 marks]
         Cluster the data set in to k-number of cluster where k is the optimum number of clusters
      for the data set, as inferred from the elbow method.


                                  4
 
                          Identify the clusters to which each data point of validation data set belongs to.
                         Print the centroid of each clusters and print the number of data points in each of the
                cluster.
                      Compute the Silhouette score of learning model.

(b) Inferences Based on the experiments, answer the following:                             [10 marks]

          i. Predicting the new output                                                                 [5 marks]
        A. You have the test data set called: D-test-data. Earlier, You have predicted the value/class
              for this test-data. Append the output E1,E2,E3, E6,E7,E8 (any two from E6,E7,E8) as
            the last five columns of D-test-data. Now, the 10-th, 11-th, 12-th columns will be numerals
          and the 13-th, 14-th columns are labels.
        B. Change the numerals of 10-th, 11-th 12-th columns as labels, as done in the Experiment
           E4.
        C. Now, D-test-data will have only labels from 10-th column to the 14-th column and the first
           9 columns are the input attributes.
       D. Predict the new label for input (each row) of the D-test-data as follows.
                     New output of an input is the median of the labels in the columns from 10-th to 14-th
             columns.
                        For example, if an input has the labels: A,B,B,C,D, the new ouptut will be B.
                      Append a new column called ’new-output’ for the dataset D-test-data and this column
                will have the new-output of all the rows of D-test-data.
                         Print the new-data-set which has 15 columns
         ii. Record all the accuracy of all the experiments in the form of a tables as follows:     [5 marks]

             ModelAccuracy                                Train data   Validation data
              Experiment 1 (Regression in Stochastic mode)
              Experiment 2 (Regression in Batch mode)
              Experiment 3 (Regression in Mini-batch mode)
              Experiment 6 (Logistic Regression)
              Experiment 7 (Decision Tree)
              Experiment 8 (SVM)

       Based on the above table, Record your inferences (as much as you can) on all the above
        exepriments.
